newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - US debt vols mostly up in cautious trade.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - US debt vols mostly up in cautious trade.

text.p: Implied volatilities for U.S. debt options were mostly firmer in thin, shortened trading as underlying markets continued rallying to fresh highs amid persistent concern about a major correction, dealers said.
Implied volatilities for January Treasury bond futures options rose a quarter-point to about 11.2 percent, while March was steady at 10.0 percent.
"We had a pretty good jump-around (in futures)," said a brokerage T-bond trader at the Chicago Board of Trade.
December T-bond futures touched a nine-month high of 116-11/32 late in the morning, up more than a full point.

In addition to fears of a correction in bond prices, volatilities were underpinned by caution ahead of next Monday's November National Association of Purchasing Management index and Friday's November non-farm payrolls, traders said.
Volume was light as many traders had not returned from Thursday's Thanksgiving Day holiday.
CBOT T-bond derivatives close early today at 1210 CST/1810 GMT, while Eurodollar products on the Chicago Mercantile Exchange end at 1200 CST/1800 GMT.

Early in the session, the market virtually ignored a robust 0.5 percent increase in October U.S. personal spending and instead extended gains on a weaker reading in the American Production and Inventory Control Society (APICS) business outlook index.
The APICS index fell to 46.8 in November from 49.1 in October.
A Eurodollar trader for an investment bank at the CME said the APICS number was more "forward-looking" than the spending data.
He said Eurodollar options trading was relatively slow.
"It's more of just position adjustment," he said. "The short Dec is going to be settling in just two weeks and there are some big positions in that."
Short December contracts are options based on December 1997 futures but which expire in December 1996.
Eurodollar implied volatilities were generally firmer, with at-the-money March and June contracts up about 0.2 point each to 10.8 and 15.3 percent respectively.
